title: Principal-quotient conditions for a fractional monogenic algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a normal Nagata domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], let $K$ be its fraction field, and let $0\ne x\in K$. Put $S=R[x]\subseteq K$, and assume explicitly that $R$ and $S$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (these follow from Nagata and finite type). Let $\mathfrak m$ be a maximal ideal of $S$ containing $x$, put $A=S_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and let $t=x/1\in A$. An associated prime of $A/tA$ means a prime equal to the annihilator of a nonzero class. Then (i) each associated prime is minimal among primes containing $tA$; (ii) $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] for each such associated prime $\mathfrak p$; and (iii) $A/\mathfrak p$ is analytically unramified [def-weil-pbc-analytically-unramified], meaning that its maximal-ideal-adic completion is reduced.

proof.text: For an associated prime p of A/tA, use the associated-localization comparison to obtain a height-one prime q of R and A_p ≃ R_q. Krull dimension is preserved by this ring equivalence and equals prime height on a prime localization. Thus p.height = 1. The normal one-dimensional local domain R_q is regular; transport regularity along the equivalence.

The generator t is nonzero because S embeds in K and localization at m is injective. Every associated prime p contains (t), by its annihilator. If a prime q containing (t) were strictly below p, it would be nonzero and hence have height at least one. Strict prime inclusion increases height by at least one, contradicting p.height = 1. Therefore p is minimal over (t).

For any ideal p containing t, put q = p ∩ S. The shared adjoin quotient-surjectivity theorem proves the map R → S/q is surjective, since x maps to zero. Hence S/q is finite over R and Nagata. The quotient A/p is isomorphic to the localization of S/q at the image of S minus m, by quotient-localization compatibility and extension-contraction. Apply Nagata localization and transport Nagata through these explicit ring equivalences using finite ascent.

When p is associated, p is prime. Thus A/p is a Noetherian local Nagata domain. Apply the local Nagata analytic-unramifiedness theorem, and identify its maximal ideal with the image of the maximal ideal of A under the quotient map.
